topics.title: The skills all candidates must develop

outcomes.text: Record personal experiences and observations using first-hand, secondary and personally researched sources.
Collect, record and respond to visual information through varied techniques.
Select, contextualise and organise collected information coherently.
Use diverse resources effectively and apply gathered information to develop artistic practice.
Carry out personal investigations.
Apply varied skills to create art and design work.
Critically evaluate work within context, incorporating personal and others’ opinions.
Reflect on, refine and adapt artistic or design work.
Use suitable materials and techniques effectively to communicate intended ideas.
Show understanding of form, function and colour relationships during the design process.
Create designs that thoughtfully consider texture, pattern and shape.
Use specialist textile processes effectively, including construction, dyeing, printing, batik, embroidery and machine stitching.
Respond appropriately to a theme or brief.
Understand the intended audience for the work.
Use visual language appropriately.
Understand suitable materials, processes, technologies and resources for textiles and fashion.
Understand how textiles and fashion design communicate ideas.
Understand the importance of location and space when making, exhibiting and viewing work.
Understand how social and cultural factors influence making, exhibiting and viewing work.
Understand the origins, continuity and development of textile and fashion techniques, genres and key movements.
Understand how intention, research, realisation and reflection contribute to textile and fashion design.
Know relevant textile and fashion genres, styles and techniques used by past and present designers.
Use specialist vocabulary relevant to textiles and fashion.

warnings: grade A Level has no content
